subject: dsa
title: Interleaving String
summary: dp[i][j] is true when s3's first i+j characters can be formed by interleaving s1's first i and s2's first j. A cell is true when the matching neighbour above or to the left is true and its source character equals the next character of s3.
problem: Decide whether s3 = "acbd" is an interleaving of s1 = "ab" and s2 = "cd". Rows are prefixes of s1 ("", a, ab); columns are prefixes of s2 ("", c, cd). dp[i][j] = true if (s1[i-1] equals s3[i+j-1] and dp[i-1][j]) or (s2[j-1] equals s3[i+j-1] and dp[i][j-1]).

steps.caption: Rows are prefixes of s1 "ab", columns are prefixes of s2 "cd", and the target is s3 "acbd". Empty plus empty makes the empty string, so the top-left is true.
Fill the base row and column. "ac" is built down column 0 by taking only from s1, but "c" then "cd" cannot start "acbd" from s2 alone.
Cell (a, c) is true because the left neighbour is true and s2's c matches s3's second character. Cell (a, cd) stays false.
Fill the bottom row. (ab, c) is true from the cell above, and (ab, cd) becomes true because d matches s3's last character with a true left neighbour.
The bottom-right cell is true, so "acbd" interleaves "ab" and "cd".
